messages:
Anna: Heads-up — SAST flagged a missing RBAC check on /admin/batch in PR #8921. Also noticed the service principal calls KMS without audit-annotating the request. Can someone triage? :eyes:
sec-bot: SAST scan complete for PR #8921 — 1 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM. See summary: auth/middleware.go: missing role check (HIGH). Link: https://ci.redwood.internal/scans/8921
Devon: thanks, looking now. quick question — is this the new batch importer?
Anna: yes, new endpoint that runs tenant-scoped batches. PR author forgot to call authorizeForTenant() before queueing jobs.
Sri: If jobs are queued without tenant RBAC, that's an auth bypass risk. Can you paste the code snippet?
Anna: paste: ```go
// auth/middleware.go
func EnsureAdmin(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
  return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    // TODO: role check missing for batch endpoints
    ctx := context.WithValue(r.Context(), "user", r.Header.Get("X-User"))
    next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(ctx))
  })
}
```
Olga: oh that TODO is new. PR diff shows middleware was refactored last week. Likely missed an inline policy call.
Frank: on the KMS side, what did you see? audit log missing how?
Anna: the code uses the default keyring client without attaching request metadata. In KMS we expect key usage to include resource_id and requestor for auditability. Current call: `kmsClient.Decrypt(ctx, ciphertext)` — no attributes.
Devon: we should treat this as P1 for compliance. If a tenant can trigger decrypts without resource tags, audit trail won't map to tenant.
Sri: Agreed. Short triage plan: 1) Mark PR as security-blocking; 2) Add RBAC check in middleware (ensure tenant+role); 3) Add KMS audit annotations in kms client wrapper; 4) Add unit + integration test for job queue mapping.
Anna: I can push a small middleware patch and tests. Also propose adding a pre-merge hook that fails SAST HIGH findings and prevents merge until acknowledged.
Olga: we already block merges for HIGH, but this slipped because scan suppression was accidentally added in the repo config. I'll remove the suppression and file a quick rollback PR.
sec-bot: NOTE: suppression removed from repo config by olga at 6501234250. Active HIGH gating restored.
Frank: For KMS metadata, we have a helper: `kms.WithAudit(attrs map[string]string)` — use that and include tenant_id, request_id, pr_author. Example: ```go
ctx = kms.WithAudit(ctx, map[string]string{"tenant_id": tenantID, "requestor": userID})
resp, err := kmsClient.Decrypt(ctx, ciphertext)
```
Devon: nice. Also let's add an automated check in the SDLC checklist: if code calls KMS.Decrypt/Encrypt, CI should assert audit attributes are set (simple linter pattern).
Sri: I'll open an issue in sec-workflows to add the linter and a short runbook for oncall. Tagging @oncall for awareness.
Anna: filing the immediate PR now. Will ping when ready for review.
Olga: please also add a repro test that simulates cross-tenant enqueue to catch regressions.
Anna: on it. ETA ~60m.
Frank: after patch, we should run a DAST smoke for the endpoint to ensure job queue paths can't be exploited.
Devon: agree. Anna, want help with the tests?
Anna: yes please — @devon can pair on the integration test.
Sri: thanks team. For process improvement: propose adding a tiny checklist item in PR template: "Does this change touch auth, KMS, or job queueing? If yes, attach security reviewer and tests." That should cut these slips down.
Olga: +1. I'll update the PR template and notify eng-committers.
sec-bot: Follow-up: PR #8921 marked security-blocking by sri at 6501234390.
Anna: PR opened: https://git.redwood/internal/p/8921 — patch includes middleware fix + kms audit wrapper + tests. Requesting sec review from sri/olga.
Frank: quick thumbs when deployed: monitor KMS audit logs for decrypt events with tenant_id populated for a while.
Devon: will add dashboard alert if tenant_id missing in decrypt events for 24h window.
Anna: thanks all — closing this thread once PR merges. :thumbsup:
